newsitem.title: USA: U.S W.Coast gasoline firms amid dimininshed stocks.
newsitem.headline: U.S W.Coast gasoline firms amid dimininshed stocks.

text.p: Wholesale prices for California-grade gasoline rose moderately Thursday, reflecting rumors of shrinking supplies and higher futures markets, traders said.

Traders said prices are beginning to reveal the high volume of cargoes exported from northern California since May. Traders say about 10 cargoes, or 2 million barrels of product, have been shipped from the West Coast to take advantage of better prices in the Far East and eastern U.S.

Closer to home, a 60-cent-price for conventional gasoline in Vancouver, Canada, has drawn California cargoes. With Los Angeles conventional grade selling around 56 cents, the prices in Canada offset transportation costs of 3.5 cents to four cents a gallon.
"Overall, everyone's realizing the (Los Angeles) market is not as well supplied as it was," traders said.
As California refiners increase conventional production to send north, the state-mandated grade, CARB, will drop in volume and raise spot prices.

Traders said pipeline prices also tightened amid rumors of a shut hydrotreater at Exxon's Benecia refinery in northern California. Traders heard from Exxon that the unit experienced a "blip" but said no further information was available.
Exxon declines comment to the press.
Meanwhile, unleaded gasoline prices on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) rose 1.43 cents a gallon to 61.89 cents. NYMEX energy prices generally influence the West Coast spot markets.
Traders offered July and August CARB gasoline to Los Angeles refineries between 60 cents and 61 cents a gallon, traders said, about 2.00 cents over Wednesday.
CARB diesel was talked between 56 and 57 cents a gallon, flat from yesterday. Jet fuel stood 55/56 cents, also unchanged.
State-mandated CARB gasoline edged up relative to L.A., ranging between 61 and 62 cents a gallon. CARB diesel fuel remained about five cents under L.A.
